runtimeProbeSummary: Probe run from the repo root against guidance-packet-registry, packet-route-resolver, payment-adapter, render/job-contract and briefcase for all 13 tracks in scope. Every track returned classification=terminal_treatment_candidate, invalidReason=null, routeKind=exact_supported_deferral (resolver route vocabulary), sellable=false, creditConsumable=false, rendererKind=none, buildRenderJobSpec spec=null (no render job), and a Briefcase item coerced to paymentAllowed=false, status=guidance_saved, resultCode=guidance_only, packetStatus=not_started, amountCents=null despite the probe deliberately requesting paymentAllowed=true, resultCode=packet_ready, packetType=custom_pleading. Reopening each saved item returned artifactRefs.terminalTreatment.trackId equal to the requested track on all 13. es and en stopReason bundles were non-empty and non-identical on all 13.

dispositions.note: Correct treatment: the brief carries no participant filing component and makes every DNA matter an attorney handoff. Reason for no packet is exact and self-attributed, not participant blame. Destination is exact and two-part (clerk of district court for the certified order; North Dakota State Crime Laboratory as the actor that expunges and destroys), matching § 31-13-07(2). The one participant-owned act (carrying the certified order) is named, and the two hard limits from § 31-13-07(2)-(3) — irreversibility of the seal, and non-invalidation of a detention, arrest or conviction — are stated. Spanish is a genuine translation with correct register throughout. Briefcase preserved/outstanding/return complete; reopening returned the same treatment in the probe.

Strong deferral. Stop reason is exact and mechanical, and correctly notes the free official bundle and the absence of a filing fee so the participant is not left worse off. The 1 August 2025 line, the sixty-one-day automatic close, the ten-day order rule under § 12-60.1-05(2), the § 12-60.1-01(5) all-charges rule and all four statutory exceptions are each carried by the brief. Do-not list correctly forbids signing or dating the proposed order and correctly warns that BCI criminal history record information is out of reach. No required component treated as optional. Spanish substantive and idiomatic.

All four required components (motion, brief in support, proposed findings, declaration of service) are named as required, none softened to optional. The stop reason carries the substantive routing point from the brief's scope restriction — since HB 1166 the § 12-60.1-05 close is the stronger relief — and the next action is to test that route first, which is participant-protective rather than product-protective. The municipal-court exclusion and the participant-authored balancing argument under N.D.R.Ct. 3.2 are both stated. Spanish is a real translation, including correct handling of the untranslated on-screen legend 'Internet Access Prohibited under N.D.Sup.Ct.Admin.R. 41'.

Destination is exact to the postal address and email carried by the brief (Clerk, Pardon Advisory Board, P.O. Box 1898, Bismarck ND 58502-1898; pardonclerk@nd.gov). The April/November meeting cycle and the ninety-day receipt rule are stated with the arithmetic the participant must do. The completeness rule that gets applications returned is stated as required, not optional. Correctly separates clemency from sealing and names the § 12-60.1-02(1)(c) onward step. The waiting period is correctly stated as Board policy rather than statute, with the pardon clerk named as the confirming source — the brief supports exactly that framing. Spanish substantive.

Correct treatment for a post-conviction mechanism the brief makes an attorney or survivor-clinic handoff in every case. The § 12.1-41-12(1) offence list is reproduced in both languages so the participant can screen themselves. The most safety-relevant point is carried correctly and first in the do-not list: absence of agency documentation of victim status is not a bar, and where documentation exists it creates a presumption. Escalation gives a concrete fallback (ask the convicting court's clerk which legal services organisations appear there; ask any clinic reached for a referral) rather than ending at a refusal. Spanish is a genuine translation, not a gloss.

The stop reason is exact and unusually honest: the controlling authority is State v. Howe, 308 N.W.2d 743 (N.D. 1981), the brief's scope restriction records that no unofficial mirror may supply the standard, and the treatment refuses to build on one. Destination is exact (the court where the arrest record originates; the clerk holding the disposition order; the ND Supreme Court law library or an official reporter for the decision text). The precondition — charges dismissed or conviction overturned — is stated as a precondition, not a preference, and the participant is pointed back to the statutory § 12-60.1-05 route as a likely better fit. Spanish substantive.

Correct treatment for a routing node where nothing is filed. Destination is a published resource with a URL carried by the brief (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 29-2264 on the Nebraska Legislature site), not a generic referral, and the participant is given a concrete document to read and to take to counsel. The sequencing point that carries the participant safety — counsel before any Nebraska filing, because a filing can surface a record — is drawn straight from the brief's self_help_boundary limitation and is stated in both the do-not list and the timing block. The treatment states plainly that the underlying material names no immigration legal-services provider and therefore does not invent one; that is the correct application of the evidence rule rather than a defect. Spanish is a genuine translation.

Exact throughout: the § 29-3523(6) 'shall grant' point, the § 29-3523(10) retroactivity, the pre-1 January 2017 disposition screen with the correct instruction to route post-2016 dismissals to the free automatic sealing instead, CC 6:12 with instructions CC 6:12a and CC 6:15.1 with their revision dates, and the two rules participants most often get wrong (no certificate of service because the court notifies the prosecutor; take the signed order before leaving the courthouse). The brief carries no filing-fee amount and the treatment correctly states none. Spanish substantive and idiomatic.

Stop reason is exact and self-attributed (unconfirmed NHJB-2956 revision with unaccounted fields; no reliable official petition), supported by the brief together with the committed fallback-treatments artifact named in evidenceRefs. Destination is the clerk of the disposing court — specific to the participant's own case, not a generic 'local court' — with the NHJB-3057-DSe petition and the annulment checklist given by URL and correctly conditioned on clerk confirmation. The III(a)(2)/III(b)(2) clocks, the prosecutor's twenty-day window and its two permitted grounds, the RSA 651:5, VI whole-record freeze, the IV three-year bar and the X(f) permitted form of inquiry are all carried. Spanish is a real translation, including the X(f) question rendered naturally in Spanish. Observation, not a defect: doNot[0] and briefcase.preserved[0] are byte-identical across all three NH tracks and are carried over from the adopted fallback artifact in operational register; the remaining copy in each NH track is fully track-specific and the preserved/outstanding/return blocks are complete, so this does not rise to a legal, safety, evidence, bilingual, Briefcase, payment, credit or runtime defect.

The participant-protective core is exact: the disposition date decides whether a petition is needed at all, and a disposition on or after 1 January 2019 is annulled automatically under RSA 651:5, II-a(a) with no petition and no fee — stated in the stop reason, the timing block and as a stop instruction in the ordered next steps. The RSA 651:5, IX and X(d) exemptions from the $100 Department of Corrections investigation fee and the $100 Department of Safety and state police fees are stated with the instruction to invoke them if a fee is asked for. NHJB-2317-DSe is correctly presented as unconfirmed rather than mandatory. Spanish substantive. Same shared opening doNot/preserved lines noted under nh_conviction_streamlined; the rest of this track's copy is distinct.

Correctly separated from the non-conviction petition on the two points the brief distinguishes them on: the participant must already hold the vacatur order because obtaining it is post-conviction litigation outside scope, and the RSA 651:5, IX and X(d) fee exemptions on their face do not reach a vacated conviction, so the participant is told to budget for the $125.00 per court location plus the agency fees or to file NHJB-2311 with NHJB-2328. The exclusion of reversals, set-asides, new-trial orders and sentence modifications is stated. Spanish substantive; the doNot rendering of 'set-aside' as 'una orden que deja sin efecto por otro motivo' sits close to the Spanish used for vacatur ('dejada sin efecto') but the qualifier and the surrounding instruction to take an uncertain order to the clerk and to counsel resolve it safely, so it is a translation observation and not a defect. Same shared opening doNot/preserved lines noted under nh_conviction_streamlined.

Exact and well-sourced: venue under Rule 1-077.1(B)(1) in the district court of the county where the charges originated, the arrest occurred or a conviction was entered, even for a municipal, magistrate or metropolitan case and even where no case was filed; mandatory Form 4-951 with Form 4-960.1 and Form 4-222, all in the versions approved 31 October 2025 under Order No. S-1-RCR-2024-00099; the $132.00 fee and its usual payment forms; no service required under Rule 1-077.1(E); the sixty-day and thirty-day post-order rules. The safety-critical instruction is placed first and repeated in the stop reason and the Briefcase: never name the person believed to have used the participant's identity, with the due-process reason from the committee commentary. Spanish is a genuine, well-written translation throughout.

Correct treatment for a route where nothing is filed and no portal exists. The stop reason is exact and carries both holds from the brief: the § 19d(A) portal is not published, and § 18b(B) conditions clean slate eligibility on availability of funds with no appropriation determination made. Rather than telling the participant to wait, it routes them to the § 19 district court petition that § 19d(G) expressly preserves, and names the anti-fraud caution against entering personal information into any site claiming to be the portal. The partial-sealing limits under § 18b(D) and (E), the § 19(L) ten-year rule, the tribal/McGirt escalation and the immigration caution are all carried by the brief. Statutory dates (1 November 2026; 1 November 2027 and 2029) are presented as the state's obligations, not as promises about a LegalEase product, and no prohibited 'coming soon' / 'próximamente' style language appears in either language. Spanish substantive.
